Area.evidence_source: Both theoretical models and research findings have examined the relationship between maladaptive perfectionism and suicide. Blatt (1995) and Burns (1980) argue that suicide is a potential outcome of maladaptive perfectionism and that the elevated rates of suicide among some professional groups may be explained, in part, by perfectionist thinking. Recently, Bell, Stanley, Mallon, and Manthorpe (2010), in a case study of the suicides of three high-achieving students, suggested that maladaptive perfectionism may explain the path to suicide.
